10.1e — 3-Button Jam: Revisions & Polish

Playtesting without revising is just collecting bad news. Today you work straight down your 10.1d triage list — fixing bugs and clarity issues first, confirming with a friend that your revision actually solved the confusion, and only then adding polish and freezing the build for Semester 1 Showcase.

Step 1 — Execute P0 & P1 Revisions (~30 min) ~30 min
  1. Fix P0 blockers cleanly: resolve any soft-lock, off-screen trap, or retry-state leak where scores/timers fail to reset on SceneManager.LoadScene().
  2. Revise for first-10-second clarity (P1): if two testers missed Button 3 or misread hazards, fix the root cause in-game (bigger key prompt on HUD, higher color contrast between walkable vs lethal objects, slightly forgiving starting speed or wider safe zone on wave 1).
  3. Verify with a Follow-Up Friend Check (mandatory): ask one of yesterday's testers to play strictly after your revision lands. Never assume your fix worked — watch them hit that exact moment again cleanly.
Step 2 — High-Leverage Feedback Polish & Freeze (~25 min) ~25 min

Once your P0/P1 verification test passes, pick two or three crisp feedback upgrades (not five new features!) that make your three buttons feel great:

  • Input response: tiny scale pop, color flash, or animation frame on the exact frame a button fires.
  • Readable threat & score pops: distinct color change on hit, clear 0.3s warning flash before hazards fire, and unmistakable score increment.
  • Zero-friction loop: brief victory/loss state → instant single-button retry tested three times back-to-back.
Feature freeze rule: do not invent a brand-new mechanic on revision/polish day or refactor working systems right before Showcase. Every post-revision tweak MUST be re-played from Launch to Retry before you commit.

Socratic: Proving That a Revision Worked

  1. Describe one P0 or P1 problem from your friend playtest, the exact code or scene change you made to revise it, and what happened differently when a tester re-played it.
  2. Did any revision accidentally introduce a side effect or new regression when you re-tested? How did re-playing catch it?
  3. Which single polish change (flash, scale feedback, sound cue, clearer HUD label) made the biggest jump in how your 3-button controls feel?

Checkpoint — before Showcase:

  • Ship every P0 and P1 revision from your friend playtest contract
  • Verify your top revision in a follow-up test run with a classmate
  • Add readability/feel polish without breaking the 3-button rule
  • Run a clean full-loop smoke check (Start → Play → Win/Lose → Retry) and commit + push
